method: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on the exact hot-path SQL, before migration 0057 / reader cutover and after, same corpus (cinema, the largest: 67 extract-stage artifacts of 108 total), same live database, no data changes between measurements other than the migration + backfill under test.

before.plan: Seq Scan on artifacts a ... Filter: (jsonb_exists(payload, 'llm_extraction') AND stage = 'extract')
before.buffers: shared hit=1573 read=45346 written=2 (~354 MB touched)

after.plan: Seq Scan on artifacts a ... Filter: (extract_stats_present AND stage = 'extract')

before.plan: Hash Join on artifacts (Seq Scan, jsonb_exists filter) x outbox_events (Seq Scan)
before.buffers: shared hit=6339 read=46857 written=7 (~362 MB touched)

after.plan: Nested Loop: Seq Scan on artifacts (extract_stats_present filter, no TOAST) x Bitmap Heap Scan on outbox_events using outbox_events_run_type_idx

controls_checked_for_regression.verdict: unchanged order of magnitude from the prior CONTROL-PLANE-HONESTY-V1 session (register 11.211) — not regressed by this migration

found_but_out_of_scope_for_this_gate.what: corpus_document_summaries()'s NON-extraction counters (chunks-by-tier, map-eligible-parents) still cost ~150ms end-to-end on cinema specifically
found_but_out_of_scope_for_this_gate.root_cause: NOT a TOAST/JSONB issue — EXPLAIN shows a Seq Scan on `chunks` (96,391 rows / 215 MB) IS the planner's correct choice here because cinema's 67 documents own 84,152 of those rows (87% of the whole table); an index scan would cost MORE at that selectivity. `chunks_doc_idx (doc_id, chunk_index)` already exists and is not being ignored — it is correctly unused for this selectivity.
found_but_out_of_scope_for_this_gate.why_not_fixed_here: This is a genuinely different problem (proportional to a corpus's raw chunk volume) from the artifacts.payload TOAST detoasting this gate targets, and fixing it would mean designing a NEW maintained summary/cache for chunk counts by document — a real, separate migration decision (semantic inventory, write-path, backfill, parity) this authority's own non-goals list warns against bundling in ("do not use this task as justification to redesign... do not refactor X merely because it happens to be nearby").
found_but_out_of_scope_for_this_gate.disposition: Documented for a future, separate slice if the owner wants corpus_document_summaries's non-extraction counters optimized too; not part of the mandatory completion gate for THIS migration, which is scoped to artifacts.payload.

outbox_events_scoping.finding: No unscoped-then-filtered anti-pattern exists in the current code for either target reader. corpus_document_summaries's extract-join already scopes outbox_events by doc_id IN-list before/during the join (not after a broad aggregate), and outbox_events is small (2,486 rows / 12 MB total) — EXPLAIN shows sub-2ms cost via outbox_events_run_type_idx (run_id, event_type) even before this migration. No index change was made: phase H's own instruction ("add the narrowest justified index only if the plan needs it") was followed by NOT adding one, since the plan does not need it.
